title: Patch: Parameterise It
story: You found the open query. Now close it.
goal: Rewrite find(db, name) so it uses a placeholder.

tests.label: Finds a real user
tests.expr: (lambda c: (c.executescript("create table users(id integer, name text); insert into users values (1,'asha'),(2,'ravi');"), [r[0] for r in find(c, 'asha')])[1])(__import__('sqlite3').connect(':memory:'))

tests.label: Attack finds nothing
tests.expr: (lambda c: (c.executescript("create table users(id integer, name text); insert into users values (1,'asha'),(2,'ravi');"), find(c, "x' OR '1'='1"))[1])(__import__('sqlite3').connect(':memory:'))

tests.label: Another attack hidden
tests.expr: (lambda c: (c.executescript("create table users(id integer, name text); insert into users values (1,'asha'),(2,'ravi');"), find(c, "' OR 1=1 --"))[1])(__import__('sqlite3').connect(':memory:'))

hints: Put ? where the value goes and pass the value as a second argument to execute.
db.execute("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?", (name,))

def find(db, name):
    return db.execute("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchall()
socratic: Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what was the bug, and how did you fix it?
solution:
def find(db, name):
    return db.execute("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchall()
